title: PEEP vs. ZEEP in Out-of-Hospital-Cardiac-Arrest
official: Peri-Arrest Ventilation With Positive End-Expiratory-Pressure vs. Zero End-Expiratory-Pressure in Out-of-Hospital-Cardiac-Arrest
summary: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major cause of mortality, with low survival probabilities to hospital discharge. Despite the frequent use of airway management and mechanical ventilation during resuscitation, there is limited evidence regarding the optimal ventilation strategy to improve oxygen delivery and patient outcomes. The present study aims to investigate the effects of positive-end-expiratory-pressure (PEEP) set at 5 mbar compared to zero-end-expiratory-pressure (ZEEP) on the return of spontaneous-circulation (ROSC) in adult patients with OHCA.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults \>= 18 years
* non-traumatic OHCA
* mechanical ventilation via airway device

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients \< 18 years,
* traumatic cause of OHCA,
* no cardiac arrest, withholding of resuscitation (e.g. Do-Not-Resuscitate orders)
